key_insight: StatLoRA reframes LoRA rank allocation as hypothesis testing, using p-values to keep the most statistically significant components under a fixed rank budget.
engineering_relevance: It offers a principled way to distribute limited adaptation capacity across layers and modules, improving parameter efficiency without relying only on heuristic importance scores.
method: Model each LoRA component with a test statistic derived from optimizer-trajectories theory.
Estimate p-values from asymptotic distributions to decide retain vs. prune under a rank budget.
Use central limit theory to justify the testing procedure for optimizers including AdamW.
evidence_signal: The method was evaluated on LoRA fine-tuning of DeBERTaV3-base, BART-Large, and Qwen2.5-7B across NLU, NLG, and QA tasks, where it matched or outperformed vanilla LoRA, AdaLoRA, and IGU-LoRA at comparable rank budgets.
watch_item: The approach depends on asymptotic normality and empirical p-value estimates, so performance may be sensitive to finite-sample effects and implementation details of optimizer dynamics.
paper_title: Statistical Inference for Rank Allocation in Low-Rank Adaptation
